description: Compute, memory pressure, persistent storage, RAID and temperature for Loem and Note. Select one or several hosts to compare workloads.

panels.description: Average across logical CPUs; includes time waiting for I/O. Current value uses only source samples received within two minutes; missing telemetry is unavailable. Historical charts use the selected time range separately.
panels.title: CPU busy

panels.description: RAM unavailable for new workloads. Linux page cache that can be reclaimed counts as available. Current value uses only source samples received within two minutes; missing telemetry is unavailable. Historical charts use the selected time range separately.
panels.title: Memory used

panels.description: Uses available bytes, including filesystem reservations; /nix/store is the same filesystem and is not counted twice. Current value uses only source samples received within two minutes; missing telemetry is unavailable. Historical charts use the selected time range separately.
panels.title: Root filesystem used

panels.description: Time since the kernel booted. Gaps are left visible when the host stops reporting. Current value uses only source samples received within two minutes; missing telemetry is unavailable. Historical charts use the selected time range separately.
panels.title: Uptime

panels.description: Average non-idle time across each host's logical CPUs.
panels.title: CPU utilization

panels.description: Available memory accounts for reclaimable page cache and buffers.
panels.title: Memory utilization

panels.description: One means one runnable or I/O-waiting task per logical CPU. Sustained values above one suggest contention.
panels.title: Load per logical CPU

panels.description: Swap capacity minus free space. Swap is a gauge; nonzero use alone does not imply an active memory shortage.
panels.title: Swap in use

panels.description: Percentage of wall time with at least one task waiting for CPU, memory or I/O. Pressure reveals contention even when headline utilization looks moderate.
panels.title: Workload pressure · waiting

panels.description: Percentage of wall time during which all non-idle tasks were stalled on memory or I/O. Sustained full stalls directly reduce useful work.
panels.title: Workload pressure · full stalls

panels.description: Excludes RAM filesystems and the duplicate /nix/store bind mount. Available bytes reflect space a regular process can use.
panels.title: Persistent filesystem utilization

panels.description: Physical devices only; RAID arrays and their partitions are omitted to avoid counting the same I/O more than once.
panels.title: Physical disk throughput

panels.description: Fraction of elapsed time with I/O outstanding per physical device. NVMe parallelism means this is an activity indicator, not a complete saturation measure.
panels.title: Disk busy time

panels.description: Number of missing RAID members. Zero is healthy. These arrays exist on Loem; selecting only Note correctly shows no data.
panels.title: RAID degraded members

panels.description: An almost full inode table can prevent new files even when byte capacity remains available.
panels.title: Inode utilization

panels.description: Synced blocks divided by array size. 100% means synchronized; this tracks resync progress when maintenance or a replacement disk is active.
panels.title: RAID synchronization

panels.description: Highest core/package reading per host. Hardware-specific throttling limits vary; use Note hardware for individual sensors and throttle activity.
panels.title: Peak CPU temperature

panels.description: Kernel out-of-memory kills during the last hour. Uses counter increases, so historical lifetime incidents do not remain as current alarms.
panels.title: Recent OOM kills

title: Fleet · system health
